mainEntity.name: How much does a Mini Countryman Cooper engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Mini Countryman Cooper engine typically costs £1,400-£3,100 supply-only, depending on generation and condition. R60 N18B16A units start around £1,400, while F60 B48A20A units range £1,500-£3,100. Used engines start from £600. Supply & fit adds £450-£950 labour. Main dealer replacement can exceed £13,000-£17,000.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure on a Mini Countryman Cooper?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common sign is a rattling noise on cold start that sounds like a diesel truck for a few seconds. As the chain stretches further, the noise becomes constant, accompanied by loss of power, rough idle and engine management lights.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mini Countryman Cooper?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Mini Countryman Cooper engine is usually worthwhile if the body, transmission and interior are in good condition. A rebuilt unit costs £1,400-£3,100 versus £4,000-£18,000 for a comparable used Countryman Cooper. With main dealer engine replacement exceeding £13,000, specialist rebuilt units offer exceptional value.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mini Countryman Cooper engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, Mini Countryman Cooper engines typically reach 120,000-180,000 miles. The B48A20A is generally more reliable than the N18B16A, particularly post-2017 units with updated timing chain design. Regular oil changes with correct BMW LL-approved specification are critical for longevity.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Mini Countryman Cooper N18 and B48 engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The N18B16A is a 1.6-litre turbo petrol fitted to the R60 generation (2010-2016), producing 120-136hp. The B48A20A is a 2.0-litre turbo petrol fitted to the F60 generation (2017-present), producing 136-192hp with improved reliability, front-mounted timing chain and better emissions compliance.

mainEntity.name: How do I find my Mini Countryman Cooper engine code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Mini Countryman Cooper engine code appears on the VIN plate under the bonnet, stamped on the engine block, or on your V5C registration document section D.2. Common codes include N18B16A (R60, 1.6L turbo) and B48A20A (F60, 2.0L turbo). Enter your reg above for instant verification.

historyTimeline.h2: Mini Countryman Cooper - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mini Countryman Cooper has been the heart of the Countryman range across two generations - the R60 (2010-2016) and the F60 (2017-present). Powered initially by the BMW-PSA derived N18B16A 1.6-litre turbocharged petrol engine, the Cooper offered a balance of performance and efficiency that defined the premium crossover experience. From 2017, the F60 generation introduced the B48A20A 2.0-litre turbocharged petrol engine as part of BMW's modular B-series family, bringing improved reliability, reduced emissions and greater refinement.

milestones.description: **2010** - R60 Countryman Cooper launched with N18B16A 1.6L turbo petrol (120-136hp)
**2013** - Mid-cycle updates to N18 ECU mapping and VANOS solenoid revisions
**2015** - Final R60 Cooper production with improved valve stem seals
**2017** - F60 generation launches with B48A20A 2.0L turbo petrol (136-192hp)
**2021** - F60 facelift with B48TU updates and revised cooling system

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every N18B16A and B48A20A engine fitted to the Mini Countryman Cooper is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Mini Countryman Cooper Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mini Countryman Cooper delivers premium driving dynamics, but its turbocharged petrol engines have well-documented weak points. The N18B16A's timing chain tensioner and turbo wastegate, alongside the B48A20A's early timing chain and cooling system vulnerabilities, dominate UK replacement enquiries. Every rebuilt Mini Countryman Cooper engine through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Failure - Why Mini Countryman Cooper N18 Engines Rattle on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The N18 timing chain tensioner loses hydraulic pressure during cold starts, allowing the chain to slap against the guide rails. Over time, the chain stretches and the plastic guides shatter, leading to valve-piston contact and catastrophic engine failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of chain, tensioner, guides and VANOS sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before rattle becomes constant; extends life 50k+ miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with upgraded timing components, new HPFP and turbo seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Permanent solution; eliminates all timing-related weaknesses

problems.recommendation: If your Mini Countryman Cooper exhibits the characteristic cold-start rattle that sounds like a diesel truck for a few seconds, address it immediately. A preventative timing chain kit is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. Once the rattle is audible at all speeds or warning lights appear, the chain has likely jumped time - at that stage, a rebuilt N18B16A engine with upgraded tensioners is the safest option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N18B16A Mini Countryman Cooper engine prices

problems.h4: Turbocharger Wastegate Failure - Why Mini Countryman Cooper Engines Lose Boost
problems.rootCause: The wastegate pivot bearings wear out over time, causing boost leaks and shaft imbalance. Direct injection carbon buildup restricts airflow, forcing the turbo to work harder and accelerating wear.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Carbon Clean & Wastegate Actuator Recalibration
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Walnut blasting of intake ports, wastegate pivot lubrication, boost control recalibration
New or remanufactured turbo with oil feed lines and intercooler inspection
repairOptions.longevity: Restores factory boost; viable if no engine damage

repairOptions.tier: Full Replacement - Rebuilt Engine with Upgraded Turbo
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new turbo assembly and revised oil feeds
repairOptions.longevity: Permanent resolution; addresses underlying oil starvation

problems.recommendation: Early turbo lag on a Mini Countryman Cooper often stems from carbon-clogged intake valves rather than a failed turbo. A professional carbon clean and wastegate recalibration typically restores performance at a fraction of the cost. If the shaft exhibits play or oil is burning heavily, however, replacing the turbo alone risks contaminating the new unit - a complete rebuilt engine is the safer long-term investment.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt Mini Countryman Cooper turbo engine prices

problems.h4: Coolant Leaks - Why Mini Countryman Cooper B48 Engines Lose Coolant
problems.rootCause: The B48 thermostat housing and coolant pipes are prone to cracking under thermal cycling, leading to coolant loss and potential overheating. This is a well-documented weakness on the B48 family.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Thermostat Housing & Coolant Pipe Replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of cracked thermostat housing, coolant pipes, system flush
Complete rebuilt unit with revised cooling system components
repairOptions.longevity: Only necessary if overheating has caused head gasket or cylinder damage

problems.recommendation: Coolant loss on a Mini Countryman Cooper B48 should be investigated immediately. Thermostat housing replacement is a relatively straightforward fix and should be addressed before overheating causes more extensive damage. If the engine has been driven with low coolant, a full rebuilt unit may be required to prevent repeat failures.
